blocks.text: Archaeology supports the presence of Persian-period Jerusalem and its administration, but it does not provide an uncontested map of this chapter’s wall route, height, or complete circuit. Proposed identifications of the gates, towers, and other locations named here therefore remain provisional.

This chapter’s long sequence of workers shows a reconstruction effort involving priests, households, craftspeople, officials, and people from surrounding areas. In the wider account, that work unfolds amid ridicule, threats, accusations, and intimidation from Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and their allies. The book also combines vivid first-person material associated with Nehemiah with third-person narrative, lists, Ezra material, and editorial transitions, so neither a purely autobiographical nor a wholly fictional reading accounts for all of its forms.

sections.title: The Building Work in Its Wider Setting
